episodes.166380: A strong storm system brought strong winds and an isolated severe thunderstorm to portions of south central Nebraska during the afternoon and evening hours of March 29th. An upper level trough deepened nearly directly over the local area during the day, which resulted in a tightening pressure gradient at the surface. Hot, dry air and resultant extreme fire conditions were pulled from the southwest up to around the Nebraska, Kansas state line. To the north, strong warm air advection led to a broken arc of thunderstorms from near Ord to Columbus between 6PM CST and 7PM CST. There was one lone severe thunderstorm in Valley County where quarter size hail was reported. Finally, as the storm system shifted east and northeast, a strong cold front moved in from the northwest and brought with it yet another surge of strong winds. Most of the wind along and behind the front was sub-severe. However, a couple 58 MPH gusts were measured at the Hastings, Nebraska airport during the mid to late evening hours. No significant impacts were noted across south central Nebraska with this event, though significant wildfires were not far to the south in north central Kansas.
episodes.167571: A strong upper-level low impacted Southern California on March 28th and 29th. Widespread precipitation occurred with this system, with areas of heavy rain at lower elevations and snow in the mountains. Heavy rain in spots led to flooding, which then led to some water rescues, road closures, as well as a small mud and debris flow on the Bond Fire burn scar.
episodes.167593: A messy complex of storms moved through the region during the overnight hours. The storms were largely below severe limits but a bowing segment produced wind damage |and a brief tornado in Rockwall County.
episodes.167841: Scattered thunderstorms moved across south central Kansas during the evening into early overnight hours of March 29th, 2022. Some of the storms produced mainly gusty and damaging winds.

events.narrative: Spotter reported storm total rainfall of 0.71 inch.

Rainfall of 0.50 inch between 7 and 8 PM. Additional 0.60 inch overnight. Additional 0.4 inch Monday afternoon. Total of 1.40 inches. Other sites near this location reported 1.40 to 2.00 inches total.
Several rock slides on Mt Baldy Road near Hill Avenue, but not enough to block the road and prevent vehicles from passing.

Vista Village Drive and High 78 off-ramp completely flooded towards bottom, reported by CHP Caltrans. No rain gauges in Vista, but Palomar-Carlsbad airport had 0.95 inch total and downstream Deer Springs had 1.27 inches.

Offramp at I-805 and Bonita Road completely flooded and vehicles were stopped before the water. Sweetwater River drainage area. 0.75 inch in 1 hour and 1.3 inches in 3 hours observed. 0.71 inch observed at Brown Field from 9 to 10 PM.
Public report of rainfall of 1.17 inch, 1mi SSE of Ramona.

A home on Calvert Rd in the Forney area sustained damage. The home lost several shingles, had broken tree limbs, and the work shop, though still standing, was structurally destroyed. Both the roll up doors were blown out and all the trusses and supports are bent and/or broken.
Thunderstorm winds damaged roofs, garage buildings, and porches to the south of McLendon Chisholm. A short tornado developed soon after.
Spotter reported storm total rainfall of 0.76 inch.
SKYWARN weather spotter reported storm total rainfall of 1.65 inches.
